Power et al. document delayed generalization on small algorithmic datasets.
Nanda et al. reverse-engineer a Fourier-based modular-addition computation in small Transformers; our architecture and measurements do not establish the same mechanism.
Liu et al. relate grokking to loss landscapes as a function of weight norm.
Varma et al. propose differing learning speeds and norm efficiencies of memorizing and generalizing circuits.
Kumar et al. study lazy-to-rich dynamics, including polynomial regression exhibiting grokking without regularization.
Davies et al. connect grokking and double descent through pattern-learning speeds and capacity variation.
Nakkiran et al. document nonmonotone generalization as model size or duration varies; the present narrow sweep does not establish double descent.
AdamW decouples weight decay from adaptive loss-gradient updates; nominal shrinkage is not a measured complete dynamical clock.
